newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq, Syria to reopen highway soon - official.
newsitem.headline: Iraq, Syria to reopen highway soon - official.

text.p: The road linking Iraq and Syria will be reopened soon to handle Iraq's imports under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, a senior Syrian businessman said in press remarks published on Thursday.
Syrian Chamber of Commerce and Industry Chairman Rateb al-Shallah said he had discussed reviving trade and industrial ties, severed since the 1980s, during his visit.
"The land highway which links Iraq and Syria would start its activity soon for the interest of both countries.

"We have come to Baghdad to establish joint cooperation and bring back normal trade and industrial ties between Syria and Iraq," the newspaper of the ruling Baath party al-Thawra quoted Shallah as saying. Shallah left Iraq early on Thursday.

Syria's relations with Baghdad deteriorated in 1980 when Damascus sided with Iran in the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran war and further worsened with Syrian troops joining the U.S.-led force which drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1991.
The U.N. deal, which went into effect in December, allows Iraq to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for its sanctions-hit population.
